subject: MAP & evaluation materials: OmniQ pilot asset exchange and acceptance cadence
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jenny Simmons <jenny.simmons@omniq.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP & evaluation materials: OmniQ pilot asset exchange and acceptance cadence

Hi Jenny —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, attached is a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (OmniQ-MAP-v1.pdf) and a small sample of the prompt pack and testcases we propose to exchange for the 30-day pilot.

High-level proposal:
- Week 0 (this week): Redwood shares a ~200-entry promptpack + 50 controlled testcases (ephemeral access).
- Week 1–2: OmniQ runs parallel acceptance checks (accuracy on core intents, latency smoke tests).
- Week 3: Joint review call to decide on full evaluation set and any redlines.
- Week 4: Closure — acceptance signoff or remediation plan.

Constraints we require in the MAP (called out in the PDF):
- Ephemeral access: test assets are hosted in a gated Drive folder; OmniQ agrees to delete local copies after 30 days unless mutually extended.
- No redistribution: assets cannot be shared outside OmniQ without explicit written permission.
- Usage: evaluation-only (no production training), aggregate metrics shareable with Redwood for improvement.

Attached for convenience: omniq-promptpack-sample.zip (small sample), omniq-testcases-2026-04.csv, and the MAP.

Next steps: can you confirm a procurement contact and whether DocuSign is preferred for the MAP? If acceptable, we can target an April 20th close for the pilot kickoff.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation materials: OmniQ pilot asset exchange and acceptance cadence

Laura —

Appreciate the clear plan and the materials. Quick clarifications from our side before we route to procurement/legal:
1) The "delete after 30 days" requirement — for our compliance team we need the option to hold a single encrypted copy for 90 days for audit only. Can Redwood accommodate a locked, encrypted audit copy retained by a named custodian?
2) Can we get a short, machine-readable manifest (CSV) that maps prompt IDs to expected labels for quicker automated acceptance tests? The sample CSV you sent is helpful but we'd prefer a normalized schema.
3) Is there a sandbox token rotation cadence you recommend for ephemeral access?

Procurement preference: DocuSign is fine. I'll loop them once legal confirms the one-off audit copy.

If you can confirm answers to 1–3, we'll aim to return redlines by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Jenny
Head of Headless Models, OmniQ
jenny.simmons@omniq.com

Jenny —

Thanks for the quick review. On point 1 (audit copy): Redwood is generally comfortable with a single encrypted, access-restricted copy retained for audit purposes only, provided that:
- The custodian is named in the MAP,
- The copy is not used to re-train models or to derive product features, and
- Audit access is logged and limited to specific people for a maximum of 90 days.

On point 2 (manifest): attaching a normalized mapping CSV in the Drive folder and we'll include a template in the updated MAP. That will make automated acceptance much faster.

On point 3 (token rotation): recommended cadence is every 48 hours for sandbox keys with a short TTL for signed URLs; we'll add explicit instructions to the Drive README.

Marissa — can you take the legal redline pass and produce a DOCX we can share with OmniQ? I'll assemble the updated MAP and manifest after that pass.

Thanks,
Karthik
